clue.text: Material Chekhov initially included in his play rewritten

indicators.note: included in means one piece is placed inside the words that follow
something rewritten has had its contents rearranged into a new order
initially points to the opening letter of the name just before it

parts.note: first letter of the Russian playwright's name

explanation.surface: A director's notes on reworking a Chekhov play, with the author slipped into the text.
explanation.walkthrough: Chekhov is a real playwright, which makes 'his play' look like a reference to The Seagull, but it is just eight letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Physical and material are synonyms as adjectives, both meaning tangible or of the body rather than the mind.

clue.text: Flower in bunch a rebel leader distributed

indicators.note: in tells you the answer is sitting inside the run of words that follows
distributed says the letters are spread across several words rather than inside one

parts.note: runs from the last letter of bunch to the first letter of leader

explanation.surface: Rebels hand out flowers from a bunch, perhaps as a peace gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' tempts you to take a first letter, but here it simply contributes its L to the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: The harebell is a wild plant with pale blue bell-shaped blooms, the bluebell of Scotland.

clue.text: Player in quartet that's been successful thus far

definitions.meaning: surface reading: a musician in a string quartet
setter's reading: one of the last four competitors left in a knockout tournament, having won every round so far

explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' and 'quartet' suggest chamber music; the quartet is really the four survivors of a knockout competition.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor reaching the penultimate round is one of four who have won all their matches to that point.

clue.text: In different senses, it may be perceived as hot or cold

indicators.text: In different senses, it may be perceived as
indicators.note: perceived through a different sense means taken in by the ear rather than the tongue, so the sound counts

parts.note: the adjective for cool weather, spelt here as the pepper

explanation.surface: A riddle about something that seems hot to one sense and cold to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Senses' means both taste and hearing: on the tongue the pepper burns, while to the ear it is the word for cool weather.
explanation.definitionFit: The pepper is fiery to taste, so hot describes it in the sense of spicy.

clue.text: Piece of wood securing pole is pine

indicators.note: securing means gripping hold of, so the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: a log is a piece of a tree trunk

explanation.surface: A carpenter describes a timber block clamping a pine post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' reads as the wood, matching the timber surface, but it is the verb meaning yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: To pine and to long both mean to yearn wistfully for something absent.

clue.text: Leaves container holding two things golfer needs, one heard

indicators.note: heard says one of the items counts by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: the peg a golfer drives from, spelt as the drink
the bag-carrier who accompanies a golfer

explanation.surface: A bag holds a golfer's essentials, one of them audible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' means tea leaves, not departs. Both items come from the golf course: the peg a ball sits on and the person who carries the clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea caddy is a small tin or box for storing loose tea leaves.

clue.text: Source of special fare husband got from old Asian city

indicators.note: got from means one piece is taken out of the bigger word that follows

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A husband brings home exotic food from an ancient city in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the husband's letter from the Indian city leaves a shop selling speciality food.
explanation.definitionFit: A deli, short for delicatessen, sells cured meats, cheeses and other speciality foods.

clue.text: Ill-defined situation with big cut covering awful year

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so one piece goes inside the other
cut means trimmed, so the word for big loses its last letter
awful suggests something in a terrible state, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a large budget cut has made for a dreadful year.
explanation.walkthrough: The trimmed word for big splits after its third letter to hold the scrambled year.
explanation.definitionFit: A grey area is a matter not clearly in one category or the other, so its rules are uncertain.

clue.text: Get to know about remaining present as stated

indicators.note: as stated means as spoken, so the word counts by its sound

parts.note: present means in this place; the spelling used is the one for listening

explanation.surface: A teacher learns about someone who stayed behind after class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift or the verb; it means being here.
explanation.definitionFit: To overhear is to learn about something by catching words not meant for you.

clue.text: Intensively study some basic education in academic stream

indicators.note: in tells you one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: the Cam is the river flowing through Cambridge, a university town
one of the three Rs: reading, writing and arithmetic

explanation.surface: Students revise hard while studying beside a river at university.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are the traditional basics of schooling, so one R is 'some basic education'. The Cam is the river in Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To cram is to study hard in a short time, usually just before an exam.

clue.text: One left area without soldier? That doesn't make sense

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a locality is a district or neighbourhood

explanation.surface: A soldier-less region is questioned: that cannot be right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside: the area wraps round the soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Illogicality is the quality of not following reason, so the definition describes it as something that doesn't make sense.

clue.text: What comes after flight — coach that's for disembarking passengers

definitions.note: read as 'a thing for disembarking passengers'

parts.note: a landing follows a flight of stairs, and also an aircraft's flight

explanation.surface: A travel guide lists what happens after a flight: a coach to take passengers onward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests a plane, but the landing is also the floor at the top of a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A landing stage is a jetty or platform where people get off boats.

clue.text: Labour's leader in mines revised leftist theory

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
revised means reworked, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: The Labour Party's leader announces a rethink of policy on the coal mines.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is the British party of the left, which fits the miners' politics of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Leninism is the revolutionary communist doctrine developed by Lenin, a theory of the far left.

clue.text: The writer and physician getting together for wine

explanation.surface: An author and a doctor meet up over a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The writer' is the setter, so it gives the first-person pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Médoc is a red Bordeaux, named after the region of south-west France where it is made.

clue.text: What ends in road rage, creating hazard

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that letter is kept

explanation.surface: A warning about how a burst of temper at the wheel makes driving perilous.
explanation.definitionFit: Danger and hazard are synonyms, both meaning a risk of harm.

clue.text: As we hear, try to escape from bloodsucker

indicators.note: As we hear means judged by sound, so the spelling may differ

parts.note: to flee is to run away

explanation.surface: Someone advises running away from a vampire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloodsucker' conjures a vampire, but it is a small insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea is a tiny jumping parasite that feeds on the blood of animals and people.

clue.text: Fellow and I modify rocket, for instance

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: An engineer and a colleague adapt a space rocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocket' suggests a spacecraft; it is the kind set off on bonfire night.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocket is one example of a firework, an explosive device lit for display.

clue.text: Land in East in fit of temper

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a flooded field where rice grows, typical of East Asia
second meaning: British slang for a tantrum

explanation.surface: Someone flies into a rage while abroad in the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a paddy' is everyday British slang for being in a temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddy is a rice field in Asia, and separately an informal British word for an angry outburst.

clue.text: Alarm about US politician that causes widespread ill-feeling?

definitions.note: the clue's 'that causes' frames the noun; ill-feeling is read as sickness

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece encloses the second

explanation.surface: A scare over an American politician whose actions spread resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ill-feeling' looks like hostility; the question mark signals it means being ill.
explanation.definitionFit: A pandemic is an outbreak of disease across a very wide area, so sickness is felt everywhere.

clue.text: Leaders of international organisation worried about state of America

indicators.note: leaders are the front letters, one taken from each word that follows

parts.note: first letters of these four words

explanation.surface: Heads of a global body are concerned about the condition of the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State of America' reads as 'condition of the country', but it is one of the fifty states.
explanation.definitionFit: Iowa is a Midwestern US state, known for farming and early presidential caucuses.

clue.text: Charts we reconstructed making case for military spending?

indicators.note: reconstructed means rebuilt in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Revised graphs make the argument for higher defence budgets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' suggests an argument, as the surface wants; it is a literal box, and the question mark flags the play.
explanation.definitionFit: A war chest is a fund set aside for a campaign, originally money kept to pay for a war.

clue.text: Ignore changes, in part

indicators.note: changes signals that the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to overlook some of the alterations.
explanation.definitionFit: A region is a part or area of a larger whole, such as a country or the body.

clue.text: Class, for example, taken to heart by one Conservative after another

indicators.note: taken to heart means placed in the middle of the words that follow

parts.note: another Conservative, a Tory being a member of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A school class is a favourite with a succession of Tory politicians.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'one Conservative after another' as C, then 'a Tory' after it. Tory is the everyday name for a British Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Category and class are synonyms, both meaning a group of things sharing a characteristic.

clue.text: Journey composer's taken after short time

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
Maurice Ravel, the French composer of Boléro

explanation.surface: A composer sets off on a trip after a brief wait.
explanation.walkthrough: The composer's name is placed after the single time letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Journey and travel are synonyms, as verbs meaning to go from place to place.

clue.text: What teacher amended, covering right way to display elements

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round another piece
amended means altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chemistry teacher corrects a pupil's way of laying out the periodic table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elements' points to chemistry, but it means the weather, as in being out in the elements.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather chart is a map showing conditions like rain and wind, which are popularly called the elements.

clue.text: Fighting men another military evacuated

indicators.note: evacuated means emptied, so only the outside letters of each word stay

explanation.surface: Soldiers are withdrawn from a second military base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evacuated' suits the military surface; here it strips the middles from both words.
explanation.definitionFit: An army is a large body of soldiers organised for land warfare.

clue.text: Part of leg held in cynical foul

indicators.note: held in means contained within the following words

parts.note: spans the end of cynical and the start of foul

explanation.surface: A footballer's leg is caught in a deliberate, cynical foul.
explanation.definitionFit: The calf is the fleshy back part of the leg below the knee.

clue.text: Top primate with cross

parts.note: X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: The leading ape in a troop is in a bad mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry; it is the letter shaped like a cross.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the highest point or tip of something, its top.

clue.text: Call on me first, in relation to treatment

parts.note: re means on the subject of

explanation.surface: A patient asks to be phoned before anyone else about their therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On me first' puts both short words ahead of the word for call.
explanation.definitionFit: Remedial means intended to cure or put right, so it relates to treatment.

clue.text: Raised voice in argument after endless decline

indicators.note: endless means without its final letter

parts.note: a set-to is a quarrel or scuffle

explanation.surface: Voices rise in a quarrel after a long slump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised voice' sounds like shouting; it means a pitch above the natural range. A set-to is British informal for a fight or row.
explanation.definitionFit: Falsetto is a male singing voice pitched above its normal register.
